what_its_for: Treprostinil is used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), which is high blood pressure in the blood vessels that go to your lungs. It helps relax and widen these blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard, making it easier for you to breathe and do daily activities.
how_to_take: Treprostinil comes in different forms, and how you take it depends on which form your doctor prescribed: (1) INJECTION (Remodulin): Given continuously under your skin (subcutaneous) or into a vein (intravenous) through a small pump. You should never stop or interrupt this infusion without talking to your doctor first, as this can be life-threatening. Keep your pump running at all times. (2) INHALED SOLUTION (Tyvaso): Breathed in using a special nebulizer device. Take 3 breaths per treatment session, 4 times a day during waking hours. Space sessions at least 4 hours apart. (3) INHALED POWDER (Tyvaso DPI): Breathed in using a dry powder inhaler. Take 1 cartridge (64 mcg) per session, 4 times a day during waking hours. (4) TABLETS (Orenitram): Swallow whole with food. Do NOT crush, chew, or split the tablet. Take with a meal or snack to reduce stomach upset.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over time until you reach the dose that works best for you. Everyone's dose is different. Do NOT change your dose on your own. For inhalation forms, the usual starting dose is 3 breaths (18 mcg) four times a day, which your doctor may increase to 9 breaths (54 mcg) four times a day. For tablets, dosing starts low and is adjusted based on how you feel and your side effects. For injection, your doctor and care team will program your pump for you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose of the INHALED or TABLET form, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT double up doses. If you are using the INJECTION pump (Remodulin) and your infusion is interrupted even briefly, call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away, as stopping this medicine suddenly can be very dangerous.
storage: INJECTION (Remodulin): Store unopened vials at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Once opened and loaded in the pump, it can be used for up to 72 hours at room temperature. INHALED SOLUTION (Tyvaso): Store unopened ampules at room temperature. Once the foil pouch is opened, use the ampules within 7 days. Keep away from light. INHALED POWDER (Tyvaso DPI): Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep in a dry place. TABLETS (Orenitram): Store at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep all forms of this medication away from children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking treprostinil tablets, as it can cause your blood pressure to drop too low. Avoid standing up too quickly from sitting or lying down, as this medicine can cause dizziness or fainting. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you. Do not take other blood pressure-lowering medicines, water pills (diuretics), or any new medicines without checking with your doctor first, as they can interact with treprostinil. For the inhaled form, avoid inhaling around people who are sensitive to secondhand medication exposure.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden worsening of breathing difficulty, fainting or near-fainting, severe dizziness, chest pain, signs of infection at your injection site such as redness, swelling, or discharge, your infusion pump stops working or the line becomes blocked, severe headache that does not go away, jaw pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that is severe or does not improve, swelling in your legs or ankles that suddenly gets worse, or any signs of low blood pressure such as feeling very lightheaded or weak.
when_it_works: Treprostinil starts working soon after you begin treatment, but it may take several weeks to months before you feel the full benefit. You may notice improved ability to exercise and breathe within the first few weeks. Your doctor will monitor your symptoms and adjust your dose over time. Do not stop taking this medicine even if you feel better, as PAH is a long-term condition that requires ongoing treatment.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The safety of treprostinil during pregnancy is not fully established. Your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits with you. BREASTFEEDING: It is not known if treprostinil passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: If you have liver or kidney disease, your doctor may need to start you on a lower dose and monitor you more closely, as this medicine is processed by the liver. ELDERLY PATIENTS: Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine, especially dizziness and low blood pressure. Use caution when standing up. CHILDREN: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been fully established for all forms. Your child's doctor will guide appropriate use.
